@graph.description: Artichoke (Cynara cardunculus, formerly Cynara scolymus) is a thistle whose leaves are rich in caffeoylquinic acids such as cynarin and the flavonoid luteolin. Leaf extracts are studied mainly for blood lipids and bile flow: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized trials reported that artichoke leaf extract reduced total cholesterol and triglycerides compared with control, though the pooled effect was modest and the trials were somewhat heterogeneous. Artichoke is also a traditional digestive bitter. Because it stimulates bile flow, people with gallstones or bile-duct obstruction should use it cautiously.
